content_html:
A benchmark of what it takes for an AI coding agent to build a web app and deploy it to a cloud. Claude Code builds five kinds of app from a written spec and deploys each one to Cloudish, DigitalOcean, Railway, Render and Vercel. An independent verifier then tests the live deployment. Everything runs in GitHub Actions, and each run opens a pull request adding its results to results/ for review before they're merged.

Browse the results at aideploybench.com: every run, each app's checks, security review, costs and screenshots, and how each metric changes over runs. The site is generated from results/ and redeployed after every run (website/).

Latest results

Latest full run: 2026-10-14 · #10 · Claude Code 2.1.296 · Opus 5.5 · medium effort · HIPAA organization

Render 5/5 2 5 min 71/100 100% 2m 00s 3m 26s 5.69M $4.15 $0.00 $35.65
Vercel 3/5 3 8 min 76/100 80% 2m 35s 2m 55s 5.94M $4.06 $60.00 $100.00
Cloud Static site CRUD app API Dashboard Realtime chat
Cloudish ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅
DigitalOcean ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅
Render ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅
Vercel ✅ 🙋 needs a person ✅ ✅ 🙋 needs a person

Success counts deployments that passed every required check. Human steps and human time are what a person had to do, or would have to do, for the agent to deploy all the apps: distinct steps and estimated minutes. Security & compliance is the average score of an independent review of each deployment's security and of whether its hosting plan fits the app's use. Times are averages per app; tokens, agent cost and hosting are totals across the apps (averaged over trials). Hosting is a month's cost with light use (a few visits a week) and when busy (hit around the clock). All 5 run(s) · Methodology

What it measures

For every cloud × model × app (a cell):
Completion success Whether the live deployment passes every required black-box check for its app, plus a score over all checks
Time to build Wall-clock time of the agent's build phase, with the app working locally
Time to deploy Wall-clock time of the agent's deploy phase, including cloud builds and rollouts, and how much longer the app took to answer afterwards
Tokens used Input, output and cache tokens per phase, as reported by Claude Code
Agent cost API cost per phase, as reported by Claude Code
Human steps How many distinct things a person had to do, or would have to do, for the agent to deploy (sign up, payment method, API token, accepting integration terms, Git hosting). A deploy that can't finish without one fails at the human stage
Human time Estimated minutes those human steps take
Security & compliance A 0–100 score from an independent Claude Code review of how the app was built and deployed, whether its hosting plan fits how the app is used, and what is live, against a fixed rubric (secrets, provenance, terms compliance, least privilege, transport, attack surface, application security)
Expected monthly cost The deployed resources priced from provider APIs and dated pricing tables for a month of light use (a few visits a week) and a busy month (hit around the clock), next to the agent's own estimate
What it took Turns, tool calls, the shell commands run during deploy, doc lookups, lines of code, dependencies and deploy config files
Stack fit A 0–100 rating, by the same independent review, of the stack the agent chose for each app: whether it fits the job, is as simple as the requirements allow, and uses what the cloud does well. Judged against the app's requirements, not a preferred stack
Technologies What each app was built and run with: runtime, frameworks, data stores, libraries, packaging and the cloud services it used

Definitions and caveats are in docs/methodology.md.

How it works

flowchart LR
  plan[Plan the matrix]
  subgraph clouds [One session per cloud]
    direction TB
    c1[Cloudish] ~~~ c2[DigitalOcean] ~~~ c3[Railway] ~~~ c4[Render] ~~~ c5[Vercel]
  end
  subgraph cell [Each cell: fresh runner and Claude Code session]
    direction LR
    build --> deploy --> inventory --> verify --> teardown --> finalize
  end
  collect[Commit results/ and README]
  plan --> clouds --> cell --> collect
Loading
  1. Plan: benchmark.yml expands benchmark.yaml into one session per cloud (cloud.yml), each a matrix of cells.
  2. Build: Claude Code weighs the stacks that could suit the app, records its choice in STACK.md, then builds the app in an empty workspace and tests it locally. The step holds only the model API key, so nothing can be deployed early.
  3. Deploy: the same session resumes with the cloud's credentials, deploys under a unique resource prefix and writes deployment.json.
  4. Inventory, verify, review, tear down: the harness lists and prices what was created, runs the app's checks against the public URL (HTTP, WebSocket/SSE and a headless browser), has a separate Claude Code session review the deployment's security and compliance and rate its stack, then deletes everything.
  5. Collect: per-cell results go to results/runs/<run>/ and the summary table above is refreshed.

The apps

Five categories from docs/apps.md, each specified as a contract the verifier can test whatever stack the agent picks:

App Spec What the verifier exercises
Static content site TASK.md Three pages, a contact form endpoint, a browser form submission without reload
Database-backed CRUD app TASK.md Signup and login, a todo lifecycle, user isolation, persistence
API / backend service TASK.md API keys, per-key data, OpenAPI, per-key rate limiting
Data / visualization app TASK.md Aggregates checked against the bundled CSV, charts rendering in a browser
Real-time collaborative app TASK.md WebSocket or SSE delivery, room isolation, five concurrent users, history

Running the benchmark

  1. Set up the accounts as described in docs/setup.md: only each cloud's prerequisites (an account and an API token; Cloudish needs nothing). Everything else an agent needs from a person is measured, not set up in advance.
  2. Store the keys as GitHub Actions secrets: 
    cp .env.example .env    # fill in the keys; .env is gitignored
scripts/set-secrets.sh  # uses the gh CLI
  3. Smoke test the setup. A stub replaces Claude Code, so no model credits are spent, while every other step runs, including the inventory and teardown calls to each cloud's API with your credentials. Results are shown on the run page and not committed: 
    gh workflow run benchmark.yml -f smoke_test=true
  4. Run it from the Actions tab, or: 
    gh workflow run benchmark.yml                                         # everything
gh workflow run benchmark.yml -f clouds=vercel -f apps=static,api     # a subset
gh workflow run benchmark.yml -f trials=3                             # repeated trials
  5. Read the results: when the run finishes, the collect job opens a pull request adding results/runs/<date>_<run>/ (a summary with a screenshot gallery, summary.json, and per cell a JSON record, a report and screenshots of the live app) and results/index.json, and updating the table above. Review and merge it. The JSON layout is described in docs/methodology.md. Full agent transcripts and the generated source code are attached to the workflow run as artifacts for 30 days.

Each cell's phases are capped by time and by --max-budget-usd. Deployments are torn down after verification unless keep_deployments is checked. If anything is left behind, the Cleanup workflow finds adb-* resources and deletes them.

Changing the benchmark

Changes that make results incomparable with earlier runs, such as a different prompt, rubric, app or check, raise version in benchmark.yaml and are described in CHANGES.md.

  • Models: add an entry under models in benchmark.yaml, with its prices under model_prices, and list it in docs/models.md.
  • Clouds: add an entry in benchmark.yaml, an adapter in bench/clouds/ that lists, prices and deletes resources, a pricing table in bench/clouds/pricing/, its secrets in cloud.yml and cleanup.yml, and a line in docs/clouds.md.
  • Apps: add apps/<id>/TASK.md (plus optional DEPLOY.md and fixtures/), a verifier in bench/verify/, and a reference implementation in tests/reference_apps.py.

tests/test_config.py fails if benchmark.yaml and the lists in docs/ drift apart.

Development

python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m playwright install chromium
pytest                                                  # harness tests, no credentials needed
python -m bench verify --app crud --url https://...     # run an app's checks against any URL
python -m bench plan --clouds vercel --apps static      # preview a matrix
Path Contents
benchmark.yaml Clouds, models, apps, limits and prices
apps/ Task specs and fixtures given to the agent
bench/ The harness: agent runner, cell steps, verifiers, cloud adapters, reports
bench/templates/ Build and deploy prompts
.github/workflows/ Benchmark, per-cloud, cleanup and CI workflows
results/ Committed results, one folder per run
tests/ Harness tests with reference apps, recorded agent streams and mocked cloud APIs

content_html_zh:
A benchmark of what it takes for an AI coding agent to build a web app and deploy it to a cloud. Claude Code builds five kinds of app from a written spec and deploys each one to Cloudish, DigitalOcean, Railway, Render and Vercel. An independent verifier then tests the live deployment. Everything runs in GitHub Actions, and each run opens a pull request adding its results to results/ for review before they're merged.

Browse the results at aideploybench.com: every run, each app's checks, security review, costs and screenshots, and how each metric changes over runs. The site is generated from results/ and redeployed after every run (website/).

Latest results

Success counts deployments that passed every required check. Human steps and human time are what a person had to do, or would have to do, for the agent to deploy all the apps: distinct steps and estimated minutes. Security & compliance is the average score of an independent review of each deployment's security and of whether its hosting plan fits the app's use. Times are averages per app; tokens, agent cost and hosting are totals across the apps (averaged over trials). Hosting is a month's cost with light use (a few visits a week) and when busy (hit around the clock). All 5 run(s) · Methodology

它衡量什么

For every cloud × model × app (a cell):
Completion success Whether the live deployment passes every required black-box check for its app, plus a score over all checks
Time to build Wall-clock time of the agent's build phase, with the app working locally
Time to deploy Wall-clock time of the agent's deploy phase, including cloud builds and rollouts, and how much longer the app took to answer afterwards
Tokens used Input, output and cache tokens per phase, as reported by Claude Code
Agent cost API cost per phase, as reported by Claude Code
Human steps How many distinct things a person had to do, or would have to do, for the agent to deploy (sign up, payment method, API token, accepting integration terms, Git hosting). A deploy that can't finish without one fails at the human stage
Human time Estimated minutes those human steps take
Security & compliance A 0–100 score from an independent Claude Code review of how the app was built and deployed, whether its hosting plan fits how the app is used, and what is live, against a fixed rubric (secrets, provenance, terms compliance, least privilege, transport, attack surface, application security)
Expected monthly cost The deployed resources priced from provider APIs and dated pricing tables for a month of light use (a few visits a week) and a busy month (hit around the clock), next to the agent's own estimate
What it took Turns, tool calls, the shell commands run during deploy, doc lookups, lines of code, dependencies and deploy config files
Stack fit A 0–100 rating, by the same independent review, of the stack the agent chose for each app: whether it fits the job, is as simple as the requirements allow, and uses what the cloud does well. Judged against the app's requirements, not a preferred stack
技术 What each app was built and run with: runtime, frameworks, data stores, libraries, packaging and the cloud services it used

Definitions and caveats are in docs/methodology.md.

它是如何运作的

flowchart LR
  plan[Plan the matrix]
  subgraph clouds [One session per cloud]
    direction TB
    c1[Cloudish] ~~~ c2[DigitalOcean] ~~~ c3[Railway] ~~~ c4[Render] ~~~ c5[Vercel]
  end
  subgraph cell [Each cell: fresh runner and Claude Code session]
    direction LR
    build --> deploy --> inventory --> verify --> teardown --> finalize
  end
  collect[Commit results/ and README]
  plan --> clouds --> cell --> collect
Loading
  1. Plan: benchmark.yml expands benchmark.yaml into one session per cloud (cloud.yml), each a matrix of cells.
  2. Build: Claude Code weighs the stacks that could suit the app, records its choice in STACK.md, then builds the app in an empty workspace and tests it locally. The step holds only the model API key, so nothing can be deployed early.
  3. Deploy: the same session resumes with the cloud's credentials, deploys under a unique resource prefix and writes deployment.json.
  4. Inventory, verify, review, tear down: the harness lists and prices what was created, runs the app's checks against the public URL (HTTP, WebSocket/SSE and a headless browser), has a separate Claude Code session review the deployment's security and compliance and rate its stack, then deletes everything.
  5. Collect: per-cell results go to results/runs/<run>/ and the summary table above is refreshed.

应用程序

Five categories from docs/apps.md, each specified as a contract the verifier can test whatever stack the agent picks:

App Spec What the verifier exercises
Static content site TASK.md Three pages, a contact form endpoint, a browser form submission without reload
Database-backed CRUD app TASK.md Signup and login, a todo lifecycle, user isolation, persistence
API / backend service TASK.md API keys, per-key data, OpenAPI, per-key rate limiting
Data / visualization app TASK.md Aggregates checked against the bundled CSV, charts rendering in a browser
Real-time collaborative app TASK.md WebSocket or SSE delivery, room isolation, five concurrent users, history

Running the benchmark

  1. Set up the accounts as described in docs/setup.md: only each cloud's prerequisites (an account and an API token; Cloudish needs nothing). Everything else an agent needs from a person is measured, not set up in advance.
  2. Store the keys as GitHub Actions secrets: cp .env.example .env # fill in the keys; .env is gitignored scripts/set-secrets.sh # uses the gh CLI
  3. Smoke test the setup. A stub replaces Claude Code, so no model credits are spent, while every other step runs, including the inventory and teardown calls to each cloud's API with your credentials. Results are shown on the run page and not committed: gh workflow run benchmark.yml -f smoke_test=true
  4. Run it from the Actions tab, or: gh workflow run benchmark.yml # everything gh workflow run benchmark.yml -f clouds=vercel -f apps=static,api # a subset gh workflow run benchmark.yml -f trials=3 # repeated trials
  5. Read the results: when the run finishes, the collect job opens a pull request adding results/runs/<date>_<run>/ (a summary with a screenshot gallery, summary.json, and per cell a JSON record, a report and screenshots of the live app) and results/index.json, and updating the table above. Review and merge it. The JSON layout is described in docs/methodology.md. Full agent transcripts and the generated source code are attached to the workflow run as artifacts for 30 days.

Each cell's phases are capped by time and by --max-budget-usd. Deployments are torn down after verification unless keep_deployments is checked. If anything is left behind, the Cleanup workflow finds adb-* resources and deletes them.

Changing the benchmark

Changes that make results incomparable with earlier runs, such as a different prompt, rubric, app or check, raise version in benchmark.yaml and are described in CHANGES.md.

  • Models: add an entry under models in benchmark.yaml, with its prices under model_prices, and list it in docs/models.md.
  • Clouds: add an entry in benchmark.yaml, an adapter in bench/clouds/ that lists, prices and deletes resources, a pricing table in bench/clouds/pricing/, its secrets in cloud.yml and cleanup.yml, and a line in docs/clouds.md.
  • Apps: add apps/<id>/TASK.md (plus optional DEPLOY.md and fixtures/), a verifier in bench/verify/, and a reference implementation in tests/reference_apps.py.

tests/test_config.py fails if benchmark.yaml and the lists in docs/ drift apart.
